title: Find a Peak Element II
summary: In a 0-indexed m x n matrix where no two adjacent cells have the same value, identify a peak element by finding one that is strictly greater than its adjacent neighbors to the left, right, top, and bottom.
statement: In a 0-indexed m x n matrix where no two adjacent cells have the same value, identify a peak element by finding one that is strictly greater than its adjacent neighbors to the left, right, top, and bottom. Return the coordinates [i,j] of the peak element. Assume the matrix is surrounded by a perimeter with -1. Develop an algorithm that operates in O(m log(n)) or O(n log(m)) time.
constraints: The matrix has 1 through 500 rows and columns with positive values.
Return coordinates of a cell strictly greater than every existing orthogonal neighbor in O(rows*log(columns)) or O(columns*log(rows)).
hints: Within a row, choose its maximum so horizontal neighbors cannot be larger.
Compare that value with the cell directly below; move toward the larger of the two row directions.
Binary-search rows until one remains, then return that row's maximum column.
A larger vertical neighbor guarantees a peak exists in that direction, preserving the search invariant; the final row maximum is greater than all four neighbors.
editorial: A larger vertical neighbor guarantees a peak exists in that direction, preserving the search invariant; the final row maximum is greater than all four neighbors.

tests.explanation: The value four at [0,1] is one valid peak because it exceeds its left and lower neighbors.
The row-search follows larger downward values and returns the unique peak 32 at [2,2].
